observations: Per-service health is triply graphical: colored status badge with dot ('.status-badge' + '.badge-dot'), status-colored 3px left border on each '.service-card', and the summary strip's green check / yellow bang / red X icons — text ('DOWN', 'DEGRADED', 'HEALTHY') supports rather than carries it.

Latency trend and error-rate trend are drawn as canvas sparklines (metrics count 12 canvas elements, 2 per service), stroke-colored by status (red for down, yellow for degraded, blue for healthy) with a gradient fill and last-point dot.
Uptime is rendered only as a colored number ('98.90% uptime', uptimeColor thresholds at 99.9/99) — no meter, bar, or chart, so the trend/level is carried by text with a color accent.
Graphical totals from metrics: svg 4, canvas 12, badges 43, total 59 graphical indicators on the desktop idle view, against only 132 visible words.
Raw ratio: 3/4 inventory items graphical+text, 1/4 text only.
Desktop pageWords is 132 for a 6-service dashboard — the UI is numbers, labels, and charts, not prose; helperWords 0 and longLeafWords 0.
All 3 measured button labels ('1H', '24H', '7D') are 1 word; meanWords 1, maxWords 1, no longLabels.

No sentence restates what the UI shows: the only sentences are the alert '1 service down: media-worker', the error copy 'Failed to load service data' / 'Refresh failed — showing last known data', and 'Loading service data…', each carrying state the visuals alone could not.
Metric sublabels are maximally compressed: 'avg 990ms · peak 1.3s', 'avg 0.44%'.

One issue found: the 'Updated <time>' header claims a fresh update the server never confirmed — render() stamps `new Date()` unconditionally, and the async rater verified the timestamp advanced from 'Updated 01:49:41 PM' to 'Updated 01:50:01 PM' while every getMetrics poll rejected, alongside the 'Refresh failed — showing last known data' banner.
Terminology is otherwise consistent: 'healthy/degraded/down' is used identically in badges, summary labels, and the alert bar; 'Latency'/'Error Rate' label both the metric boxes and their sparklines.

No filler, no marketing tone, no placeholder text anywhere in the 132 visible words; error copy is specific ('Failed to load service data', 'Refresh failed — showing last known data') and matches what actually happened.

The information design is built for the on-call glance: render() sorts services down-first ([...down, ...degraded, ...healthy]), a red alert bar names the down service above everything else, and a Healthy/Degraded/Down triage strip gives counts before any card.
Status is encoded redundantly in color (left border, badge, latency value color, sparkline stroke) so a periphally-viewed dark screen reads correctly — dark theme suits a NOC/on-call context.
Freshness is treated as first-class: pulsing '.live-dot' titled 'Auto-refreshing', 'Updated HH:MM:SS' timestamp, and a stale-data banner on failed refresh.

The visual vocabulary itself is stock dark-SaaS-dashboard: Inter from Google Fonts, Tailwind default palette hexes (#34d399, #fbbf24, #f87171, #60a5fa), pill badges, rounded card grid — competent but recognizably template.
From the idle desktop screenshot alone, before source: purpose read instantly as a service health dashboard ('Service Health' h1, 6 metric cards with sparklines) — correct against the brief.

What needs attention was unmissable: red banner '⚠ 1 service down: media-worker', '1 Down' summary tile, red-edged media-worker card sorted into first position, amber 'notifier DEGRADED' second — exactly the at-a-glance answer the brief demands.
Primary action read as the 1H/24H/7D range toggle top-right (24H active), the correct and only meaningful action on a read-mostly monitoring page.
The empty bottom half of the 1440x900 viewport keeps all six services above the fold with zero scrolling.
